title: Janus MgAlB_2 MBene: a dipole-engineered anode for ultrafast Li-ion transport and exceptional lithium storage
authors: Pritam Samanta, Sashank Kumar Pandey, Amit Kumar Jana, Prakash Parida
abstract: In this work, we propose a group II/IIIA-based Janus MBene, MgAlB_2, and investigate its electrochemical properties using first-principles calculations. The substitution of one Mg layer in Mg_2B_2 MBene by an Al layer breaks the structural symmetry and generates a permanent out-of-plane polarization, giving rise to a distinct electronic environment compared with the parent Mg_2B_2 and Al_2B_2 monolayers. Electronic-structure analysis reveals enhanced orbital hybridization among B, Mg, and Al states near the Fermi level, resulting in improved electronic delocalization across the monolayer. The Janus MgAlB_2 monolayer is found to possess excellent dynamical, mechanical, and thermal stability. Owing to its polarization-modified energy landscape, Li ions migrate with an exceptionally low diffusion barrier of 17.1 meV, corresponding to a room-temperature diffusion coefficient of 3.43x10^-10 cm^2/s. Unlike the pristine Mg_2B_2 and Al_2B_2 monolayers, which support only a single stable adsorption layer, MgAlB_2 accommodates two complete Li layers. Detailed analysis shows that the residual polarization retained after first-layer lithiation continues to promote Li adsorption, whereas increasing Li-Li electrostatic interactions eventually limit further storage. As a result, the Janus monolayer delivers a high theoretical specific capacity of 1470.24 mAh/g together with a small volume expansion of only 3.7% during maximum lithiation. The present study demonstrates that intrinsic polarization can be utilized to regulate both the thermodynamics and kinetics of Li storage, providing a design strategy for high-rate and high-capacity two-dimensional electrode materials.
summary: This theoretical study proposes a dipole-engineered Janus MgAlB2 monolayer as a superior anode material for Li-ion batteries. By breaking structural symmetry, the material generates an intrinsic polarization that significantly lowers the lithium diffusion barrier and increases storage capacity compared to its symmetric counterparts. The work establishes intrinsic polarization as a powerful design principle for next-generation energy materials.
main_problem: The research addresses the need for novel, high-performance anode materials for Li-ion batteries that overcome the capacity limitations of conventional anodes.
main_result: The dipole-engineered Janus MgAlB2 monolayer exhibits exceptional performance, achieving a high theoretical specific capacity (1470.24 mAh/g) with ultrafast Li ion transport due to its intrinsic polarization.
method: First-principles calculations using DFT were employed to model the electronic structure, electrochemical properties, and ion diffusion kinetics of the proposed material.
model_or_system: The system is a Janus MgAlB2 monolayer, engineered by breaking the symmetry of parent MBenes structures (Mg2B2 or Al2B2) through Al substitution. This asymmetry generates a permanent out-of-plane polarization and built-in electric field.
key_observables: Low Li diffusion barrier (17.1 meV), high theoretical specific capacity (1470.24 mAh/g), dipole moment, and intrinsic polarization magnitude.
important_parameters: Room-temperature diffusion coefficient ($3.43	imes10^{-10} 	ext{ cm}^2/	ext{s}$), volume expansion ($\le 3.7\%$), and the built-in electric field strength.
main_assumptions: The calculations assume that intrinsic polarization can be utilized as a design parameter to regulate both the thermodynamics (storage capacity) and kinetics (ion transport) of lithium storage.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate optimized geometries, electronic structure analysis (PDOS/Band Structure), charge transfer mapping (EDD plots), and calculated diffusion pathways/barriers for Li ion movement.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by identifying the limitations of symmetric MBenes, proposing the Janus structure to induce polarization, and then using DFT calculations to quantify how this intrinsic dipole enhances Li adsorption capacity and accelerates ion diffusion compared to pristine materials.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state electrochemistry, the concept of engineering an intrinsic electric field via structural asymmetry (Janus effect) to control charge transport kinetics is analogous to designing quantum interfaces or controlling local potentials in AMO systems.
